messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.

Design request. I'm L3. I've got a Cesaroni M1520 sitting in my range box. Make it fly as high as is sensible, but it must come down under 6 m/s. I'd like at least 2,000 m out of it. Winds are typically 2 m/s. We launch off a 3 m rail.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: The motor is a Cesaroni M1520, and the flyer is L3 so an M is legal. At least 2,000 m, and as high as is sensible on that motor. Landing under 6 m/s. Wind is 2 m/s and the rail is 3 m, both stated, so both go on every run. Site is sea level. Drag-free speed for 2,000 m is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 2000) = 198 m/s, which an M should beat. The sim has to actually reach the ground, so the chute cannot be so big that a high coast is still in the air at the end of the run.
2. Feasibility: I need the M1520 card before I pick a tube. An M is a lot of impulse, so 2,000 m is a floor, not the hard part. The hard part is staying stable while that much propellant burns, and still touching down under 6 m/s.

2. Feasibility: Cesaroni 7579M1520-P is class M, 7579.1 N*s, 1557.6 N, 4.86 s, 98 mm by 0.548 m, 6.718 kg with 3.737 kg of propellant. It lists no delays, so the chute is electronic. 7579.1 N*s is under the 40,960 N*s cap. On a guessed 10 kg rocket, thrust-to-weight is 1557.6 / (10 * 9.81) = 15.9. A 3 m rail helps the exit speed. About a third of the mass is propellant, so the fins have to be large or the margin dies in the burn.
3. Size: For 10 kg at 5 m/s the chute is 2 * 10 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 5^2) = 8.0 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 8.0 / 3.1416) = 3.2 m. I will use 3.4 m so the landing stays under 6 m/s and a coast of a few kilometres still reaches the ground. Tube 0.110 m, mount 0.102 m, clear of the 0.098 m case.
4. Draft: Fiberglass ogive 0.35 m on a 1.15 m fiberglass tube, outer diameter 0.110 m, wall 3 mm. M1520 plugged, 3.4 m chute at apogee. Mount 0.102 m by 0.58 m. Three fiberglass fins, root 0.28 m, tip 0.12 m, span 0.18 m, sweep 0.12 m, 6 mm. Wind 2 m/s, rail 3 m.

The rail margin is 0.46 cal, and the burn minimum is 0.46 cal, so it is not stable and 4593.1 m is not a sensible maximum. Rail exit 28.8 m/s and thrust-to-weight 13.8 pass. Mass 11.5 kg. Chute at 26.4 s, which is apogee. Flight time 1018.0 s, so the chute did finish inside the clock.

5. Fix: 0.49 cal is the failure. I am adding 1.5 kg at 0.10 m from the top of the tube. Fins stay. Altitude can come down and still clear 2,000 m. Wind 2 m/s, rail 3 m.
